css-reorder-tab-vs-visual-meaning/case-0.mechanism: CSS Grid 2-D placement (grid-column + grid-row) renders a seat chart numbered 1-40 left-to-right then top-to-bottom, but the seat <button>s are emitted COLUMN-MAJOR in the DOM (all of column 1's seats, then column 2's, ...), so with no tabindex/JS Tab traverses DOWN each column (1,9,17,25,33,2,10,18,...) instead of the visible seat-number sequence, destroying the meaning/operability of seat selection.
css-reorder-tab-vs-visual-meaning/case-0.scenario: Riverbank Playhouse seat-selection chart ('An Evening of Chamber Music'): an 8-column x 5-row (rows A-E) grid of seat <button>s numbered 1-40, placed by CSS grid-column/grid-row so they ascend left-to-right then top-to-bottom. The buttons are emitted column-major in the DOM (col1: 1,9,17,25,33; col2: 2,10,18,26,34; ...). No tabindex, no JS. Tab walks down each seat column (1,9,17,25,33, then 2,10,18,26,34, ...) rather than the visible 1..40 reading order.
css-reorder-tab-vs-visual-meaning/case-0.note: Wrong concrete instance: prose described a Lakeview Dental 7-column September-2026 date-picker with weekday columns (Mon 7,14,21,28...), but the actual page is a Riverbank Playhouse theatre seat chart with an 8-column, 5-row grid of seats numbered 1-40. Same SC 2.4.3 column-major-DOM mechanism; brand, dimensions, example values, and primarySelector semantics drifted (button.col-3 = seat column 3 = seats 3,11,19,27,35, not a third weekday).

f85-revealed-dialog-not-adjacent/case-05.mechanism: F85 open branch via include-file split: the trigger (header partial) and the revealed disclosure panel (footer theme partial) are far apart in the flattened DOM, and the open handler performs no focus move (zero .focus() calls), so both F85 step-1 checks are false and the eight program links are reachable only after tabbing the whole page and footer.
f85-revealed-dialog-not-adjacent/case-05.scenario: University admissions page: an 'Explore Northgate ▾' mega-menu button in the header partial reveals a disclosure panel — a labelled <nav aria-label='Explore Northgate'> of plain <a> links (no role=menu/menuitem) — emitted by the footer theme partial, so its markup sits near the end of the DOM while position:absolute;top:96px floats it under the header to look attached; opening it only toggles .open/aria-expanded with no focus move, so the next Tab from the trigger goes to header/main-content links, not into the panel.
f85-revealed-dialog-not-adjacent/case-05.note: Page is a genuine F85 failure (no focus move on open + revealed widget far in source), but the markup uses <nav aria-label> with plain <a> links — the page comment explicitly states 'no role=menu'. The scenario/mechanism wording 'role=menu panel' / 'menuitem' is inaccurate; corrected to a disclosure-nav of plain links.

nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st.mechanism: Two focusable links per card — an absolutely-positioned 'stretched' card-cover <a> filling the whole card plus a visible 'Listen now' <a> — both resolve to the same episode destination, producing a redundant duplicate focus stop for every item.
nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st.scenario: Public-radio episode list (Tidewater FM) where each li.episode contains an absolutely-positioned a.cover link filling the card AND a visible a.listen 'Listen now' link, both pointing to the same #ep- anchor, so Tab stops twice per episode across the four-episode list (card-title link, then 'Listen now' to the identical destination).
nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st.note: Page genuinely demonstrates the per-item double focus stop (4 li.episode items), but the description prose drifted: there is no <article>, no tabindex=0, no role=link, no onclick, and no 'Read more' link, so primarySelector article.card[tabindex=0][role=link] does not exist. The real construction is the Bootstrap-style stretched-link pattern: li.episode > a.cover (whole-card) + a.listen 'Listen now', both to the same href.

nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st.mechanism: Each timed step's real 'Start … timer' <button> is nested INSIDE a focusable static badge (<span class="badge focusable" tabindex="0">) whose own accessible text already includes the nested button's wording, so Tab stops on the badge (announcing the timer action) and then again on the button itself — the same timer control appears to receive focus twice in a row. This is the Understanding note's named failure ('a control appearing to receive focus multiple times due to the use of nested focusable elements'); the doubled, confusing stop impedes operation.
nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st.scenario: Recipe 'Cook mode' page (Hearthline, slow-braised short ribs): each step's 'Start 30 min / 8 min / 3 hr timer' <button> is nested inside a focusable static badge span (tabindex="0") that hosts a coachmark on focus, so tabbing each timed step lands first on the badge (whose text already reads out the timer action) and then on the timer button — a doubled focus stop on the same control.
nested-and-static-focusable-illogical-st.note: rewritten to match the page (was a different instance)
